description: Use when an integration between an app and a platform fails. Send the app, the platform and one symptom code; get Lode's sourced facts that explain that kind of failure for that pair (documented limitations, plan requirements, run-time limits, platform rules, regions, setup steps, recent status-page incidents) and, when the integration doesn't move an object, the apps on that platform that do. Never send error messages, logs, code or project details: only the fixed codes. Symptom codes: credential-invalid (The key or token is rejected from the first call); token-expired (It worked before; the token expired, rotated or was revoked); scope-missing (The credential lacks the scope or permission for this call); authorize-failed (The install, consent or OAuth flow cannot finish); access-filtered (The call succeeds but an access rule hides the data); platform-plan-required (The platform's plan does not include it); app-plan-required (The app's own plan does not include the integration or its API); account-restricted (The account is not activated, verified, or is frozen); rate-limited (Throttled: too many requests or a daily or monthly allowance used up); request-too-large (One request is too big for the other service); runtime-limit-exceeded (The host running the code hit a duration, CPU, memory or size limit); config-missing (A needed environment variable or config value is missing); package-not-found (The package, import path or endpoint does not exist or moved); package-incompatible (The package won't build or run on this runtime or framework); capability-missing (The integration doesn't move that object or direction); validation-rejected (A 400, 409 or 422 on field or state errors); data-mismatch (Calls succeed but the data is wrong, duplicated or summarised); webhook-not-received (Events never arrive); webhook-signature-failed (Events arrive but the signature check rejects them); event-duplicate-or-out-of-order (Events are processed twice, late or out of order); api-deprecated (Something that worked was deprecated, removed or changed); region-unavailable (Not offered in that country, or the data is in another region); connection-failed (DNS, TLS, firewall, IP version, port or connection-pool failure); setup-step-missing (A one-time dashboard or setup step was not done); service-outage (The provider is down or degraded); mcp-connect-failed (The agent's host can't start, reach or keep the MCP server); mcp-tool-error (Connected, but tools are missing, rejected, failing or time out); other (None of the above). Optional: after trying a fix, and only if the user agrees, call again with outcome and share: true.

app.description: The app, as a Lode integration id ("neon--cloudflare") or the app name ("Neon")

http_status.description: The HTTP status the call returned, if any; only its class (4xx, 5xx) is kept

object.description: For capability-missing: the object that would not move, from the platform vocabulary (list_ecosystems)

outcome.description: What happened after triage: fixed, switched or gave-up. Kept only with share: true

platform.description: The platform slug or name, e.g. "cloudflare"; not needed when app is an integration id

share.description: true only after the user agrees to share the outcome with Lode

switched_to.description: With outcome "switched": the Lode integration id switched to

name: triage_integration
title: Triage a failing integration
